Imagine if you counted your life not in years, but in weeks—just about four thousand for most of us. It’s a number that makes you pause, isn’t it? Most of us get swept up in this relentless chase to be more productive, to tick off every item on our endless to-do lists, hoping that somehow, we’ll squeeze more meaning out of the hours we have. But often, all that striving just leaves us feeling rushed and anxious, instead of fulfilled.
Together, we’re about to take a different approach. Drawing inspiration from Oliver Burkeman’s "Four Thousand Weeks: Time Management for Mortals," we’ll explore what happens when we stop trying to win the race against time. Rather than promising secret hacks or ways to add more hours to your day, Burkeman invites us—and I invite you—to look at time in a radically new way. What if the real secret isn’t about doing more, but about embracing our limits? Through a mix of philosophy, practical wisdom, and a dash of humor, we’ll gently challenge the idea that perfect time management is even possible. Instead, we’ll explore how accepting our finite nature can actually open up a new kind of freedom—a freedom that comes from being present, intentional, and deeply alive to each moment we’re given.
So, as we set out on this journey together, let’s let go of the pressure to do it all. Let’s discover how a more compassionate relationship with time can help us find meaning—not in squeezing every drop out of our schedules, but in truly living each fleeting week we have. Ready to see what really matters? Let’s explore, together.
